question: Greenspan warned of irrational exuberance in December 1996, with the S&P 500 at 744. Where was it at the 2002 low?
answer: About 780. The index roared past 1,500 by 2000, then crashed, yet its October 2002 low of 777 was still above the level of the warning. Calling a bubble early can be right about the excess and wrong about the money: a seller in 1996 missed the boom and got no discount at the bottom.
move: Being early about a bubble can cost as much as being wrong.
ask: When I am sure something is overpriced, what would it cost me to be right but years early?
trap: About 450, picturing the crash wiping out the whole boom.
source: Greenspan, speech at the American Enterprise Institute
reference: Greenspan, The Challenge of Central Banking in a Democratic Society, speech at the American Enterprise Institute, 5 December 1996
